representations.text: Over 28 baseline days and 14 window days with complete wear, all metrics remained highly stable. Sleep averaged ~470 min (22:50–07:00), steps ~8000, activity ~55 min, low movement ~450 min, RHR ~56 bpm, and RMSSD ~40 ms. Window means differed by <1% from baseline. Day-to-day variability decreased slightly in the window for sleep and HRV. Activity showed a weak negative correlation with steps in baseline but not in the window. No sustained shifts or temporal structure changes were observed.

Across 28 baseline and 14 window days with full wear, most metrics were stable. Sleep averaged ~471 min (baseline) vs ~468 min (window), ending consistently at 07:00. Steps averaged ~8066 vs ~7954. Activity (~55 min), low movement (~451 min), and RHR (~56 bpm) were unchanged. RMSSD mean fell from 45.3 to 43.1 ms, driven by a single weekend drop to 23 ms on Apr 5; otherwise it stayed near 43–47 ms. Baseline RMSSD variance was very low (1.6); window variance rose to 32.8 due to that outlier.

During the 28-day baseline, daily steps averaged ~8009 with stable sleep (~470 min, 22:50–07:00), activity (~55 min), low movement (~451 min), RHR (~56 bpm), and RMSSD (~45 ms). In the 14-day window, steps dropped abruptly to a mean of ~2335 (range 2064–2636), a 71% decrease persisting throughout. All other metrics remained near baseline levels: sleep ~470 min, activity ~55 min, low movement ~453 min, RHR ~56 bpm, RMSSD ~45 ms. No gradual transition preceded the step reduction.

During the 28-day baseline, daily steps averaged ~2818 with stable sleep (~471 min, 22:50–07:00), activity (~56 min), low movement (~451 min), RHR (~56 bpm), and RMSSD (~45 ms). In the 14-day window, steps increased abruptly to a mean of ~7927 (range 7636–8320), nearly tripling and persisting throughout. All other metrics remained near baseline levels: sleep ~469 min, activity ~55 min, low movement ~447 min, RHR ~56 bpm, RMSSD ~45 ms. Low movement decreased slightly. No gradual transition preceded the step increase.
